newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends barely moved in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends barely moved in thin trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed barely moved against the dollar on Tuesday in low trade as banks were shy to quote two-way rates, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 59.27 to the dollar, after opening at its previous closing level of 59.28, they said.
"There was hardly any movement today. Banks were not willing to quote two-way prices since the exchange rate was already close to the Central Bank's selling price," said a Citibank dealer.
Commercial banks were not willing to quote two-way prices since the Central Bank has said it will sell dollars only for covering trade-backed transactions, dealers said.
The Central Bank's buying and selling prices were at 58.1081 and 59.2820.
Overnight call money rates closed at 8.5 percent, after opening at 9.5 percent and rising to 11 percent, dealers said.
"The money market is so liquid that banks covering imports with dollars from the Central Bank, are not really having an impact on call rates," said a foreign bank dealer.
Call rates have eased due to a high level of liquidity after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios by three percent this year and allowed exporters to borrow in foreign exchange.
